faq.subtitle: OKR method, habits, time-blocking, demo mode, security... we answer everything.
faq.a1: Yes, for personal use: tasks, habits, calendar, OKRs, statistics and task sharing. Only the business mode is paid, beyond five members.
faq.q2: What is the OKR method and why use it?
faq.a2: The OKR method (Objectives & Key Results) is a goal-tracking system used by Google, Intel and Netflix. Start with an overall objective (for example: get back into sport), then metrics tied to it (for example: do 15 workouts and 10 days at 10 000 steps). Finally, set an end date for reaching the objective. Cosmo calculates your progress in real time.
faq.q3: How is it different from Notion or Todoist?
faq.a3: Notion is a flexible note-taking space without a native productivity structure. Todoist is a task manager but does not include habits, OKRs or time-blocking. Cosmo brings the four pillars (tasks, habits, calendar and objectives) together in one coherent, intuitive ecosystem.
faq.a4: Click "Try the demo": you get the full app straight away, pre-filled with 100 tasks, 100 habits, 150 calendar events and 8 OKRs across 12 months of realistic data. No account, no email asked. When you're convinced, create your real account in 30 seconds.
faq.a5: Yes. Cosmo has a mobile version, but it is in beta: for now, we recommend the desktop version.
faq.q8: How do I track my habits effectively?
faq.a8: Create a habit, set its frequency (daily, weekly, specific days), then tick it off each day. Cosmo shows a GitHub-style 26-week heatmap, computes your streak (consecutive days) and your completion rate over the period you choose. The golden rule: start with 2 to 3 habits at most.
faq.a9: Your data is stored in Ireland on Supabase, with Row Level Security: another user can only reach what you share with them. Only the publisher has technical access, reserved for maintenance, security and support, and backups are encrypted. The app's pages (dashboard, tasks, etc.) are blocked for search crawlers in robots.txt. In demo mode, data stays in your browser (localStorage) and never touches our servers.

about.metaDescription: Why Cosmo exists: a free productivity app that brings tasks, habits, calendar and OKRs into a single ecosystem.
about.title: About Cosmo
about.subtitle: A free, all-in-one productivity app.
about.p1: Getting organized in 2026 too often looks like this: a to-do list somewhere, a habits app elsewhere, a calendar in a third tool, and new-year objectives… in a spreadsheet nobody opens again. Each tool is fine, but none of them talk to each other.
about.p2before: Cosmo starts from a simple conviction:
about.p2bold: personal productivity rests on four pillars: tasks, habits, time and objectives
about.p2after: , and they only really work when connected. A task gets scheduled in the calendar, a habit feeds an objective, and all of it is measured in one place.
about.principle1: The core features are free, with no artificial limits. We would rather convince you than lock you in.
about.principle2: The demo opens with no account and no email, pre-filled with 12 months of realistic data. Judge for yourself.
about.principle3: Tasks, habits, calendar and objectives are designed together from the start, not bolted on afterwards.
about.principle4: Secure storage with Row Level Security, and in demo mode nothing leaves your browser.
about.namesP: All three refer to the same app:
about.namesAfter: . People also look for us as “Cosmo app”, “The Cosmo” or “thecosmo app”, it's always us. Not to be confused with other products of the same name on mobile stores: Cosmo is a web app, with nothing to download, and its only official site is thecosmo.app.
about.founderP: Cosmo was founded by Axel Longatte, who is its publisher and editor-in-chief: the blog articles are published under his responsibility.
about.whoP: Cosmo is an independent product, built in France by a very small team: no funding round, no aggressive growth hacking, just a product we improve every week by listening to what users tell us.
about.contactP: A question, a bug, an idea? Write to us:

eisenhower.intro: Sort your tasks into the four boxes, free and with no sign-up. Everything stays in your browser: print the matrix or pick it up in Cosmo.
eisenhower.privacy: Your tasks are saved in this browser only. Nothing is sent to Cosmo.
eisenhower.ctaTitle: Turn box 2 into real time slots
eisenhower.ctaText: In Cosmo, your important tasks get a slot in the calendar, next to your habits and goals.
eisenhower.howTitle: How to use the matrix well
eisenhower.how1: Start by emptying your head: every task for the week, without sorting. Then ask two questions of each: does this move me towards my goals? Does it have to be done today or tomorrow?
eisenhower.how2: The box that matters most is the second one: important but not urgent. That is where the projects that change your quarter live. Give them a slot in your calendar before the week fills up.
